result_status: answered NO: for every weight sequence with rho = 0 and every lambda > 0 there are infinitely many n along which P(Y_(1) = m) -> 1, so Y_(1)/n -> lambda there and cannot tend to 0 along the full sequence. The per-ball rate F(s) = (f(s)+log(s/lambda)+1)/s diverges when rho = 0, hence has infinitely many records; at m equal to a record the maximiser is m itself, and the only way the allocation could fail to concentrate there is a record gap below C/sqrt(m), which chained over multiplicative blocks would force F bounded and so rho > 0.

source_title: Two problems for threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: front propagation with a Bramson correction, and the continuous-type limit theory (Achyut Kumar, Abhinav Duddala)
locator: Conjecture 3.2 (Uniform integrability of the derivative martingale ⇒ Bramson delay); Section 3.2
title: Conjecture 3.2 (Uniform integrability of the derivative martingale ⇒ Bramson delay) of arXiv:2608.21125
statement: "Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, the derivative martingale ∂W_n is uniformly integrable (equivalently, ∂W_∞>0 a.s. on survival), and consequently the time-indexed front obeys F(t)=c*t−(3/(2θ*c*))log t+O_ℙ(1), with the tightness and the limiting law of the recentred front F(t)−c*t+(3/(2θ*c*))log t given by a randomly-shifted Gumbel decorated point process, the shift being a multiple of log ∂W_∞, exactly as for branching Brownian motion."
context: This paper is an explicit companion to arXiv:2608.15987 (above), formulating precisely two problems that paper left open, supplying the analytic framework, and proving partial theorems.
result_status: source correction plus partial resolution: the conjecture's parenthetical equivalence is inverted - uniform integrability of the derivative martingale forces its limit to vanish (E[dW_n] = dW_0 = 0 and the limit is nonnegative), while nondegeneracy is what the Bramson programme needs; with the hypothesis repaired to nondegeneracy, Chen's x log^2 x criterion applies and the martingale half is a theorem in the bounded-degree dissipative regime, leaving only the decorated-point-process transcription

locator: (unlabeled, stated as "the key open question" in the Introduction); Section 1, Introduction
title: (unlabeled, stated as "the key open question" in the Introduction) of arXiv:2607.07410
statement: "the key open question: can random drift perturbations break the compactness of confining deterministic diffusion semigroups?"
context: The paper answers this affirmatively in specific regimes (Proposition 5.2) but leaves the boundary case δ>1/α genuinely open, stated in Remark 5.3 (see below).
result_status: answered for polynomial confinement: yes, a semi-selfsimilar Levy drift breaks compactness of L^{w}, for every delta > 0 and not only delta <= 1/alpha, whenever the drift has jumps of the sign that deepens the well
author: claude-prob1000-0913-20h

source_title: Essential spectrum for Brox-type diffusion processes (Yuichi Shiozawa, Jian Wang)
title: Remark 5.3(ii), first case (L^{w1+W}) of arXiv:2607.07410
statement: "For δ>1/α, we do not know if L^{w1+W} generates a compact Markovian semigroup on L²(ℝ;μ^{w1+W}). In fact, by Lemma 5.1(ii), we have Q-a.s., for any x>0, ∫_x^∞ e^{-(y^δ+V(y))} dy<∞. However, since we have no information about the decay rate of ∫_x^∞ e^{-(y^δ+V(y))} dy as x→∞, it is unclear if the left hand side of (5.6) is divergent or not as x→∞. Therefore, we could not apply [26, Theorem 2] to L^{w1+W}."
result_status: answered NO (not compact) whenever the Levy measure charges the negative half-line, hence unconditionally for alpha in (0,1) and for symmetric V; the Hardy quantity is lifted by e^m at a downward jump of size m while the potential charges only (2delta-2) log x
author: claude-prob1000-0913-20h

source_title: Essential spectrum for Brox-type diffusion processes (Yuichi Shiozawa, Jian Wang)
title: Remark 5.3(ii), second case (L^{w2+W}) of arXiv:2607.07410
statement: "On the other hand, for δ>1/α, we do not know if L^{w2+W} generates a compact Markovian semigroup on L²(ℝ;μ^{w2+W}). In fact, by Lemma 5.1(ii), we have Q-a.s., for any x>0, ∫_x^∞ e^{-y^δ+V(y)} dy<∞. Define h(x)=∫_x^∞ e^{-y^δ-V(y)} dy for x>0. In order to apply [26, Theorem 2] to L^{w2+W}, we need to calculate limsup_{x→∞} (1/h(x) − 1/h(0)) ∫_x^∞ h(y)² e^{y^δ−V(y)} dy, but this value is unknown at present."
result_status: answered NO (not compact) whenever the Levy measure charges the positive half-line, by the same argument with the jump sign reversed; for a spectrally one-sided drift exactly one of H0013/H0014 is broken and the other is compact (Theorem 3, sketch)

source_title: Extinction and Survival in an Interval-Activation Frog Model on ℤ with Random Survival Parameters and Symmetric Random Walks (Gustavo Oshiro de Carvalho, Fábio Prates Machado, José Hermenegildo Ramírez-González)
locator: Theorem 3.5(ii) and Remark 3.6, Section 3.2 (stable regime); the intake had written Theorem 5(ii) / Remark 6
title: (unlabeled open gap, Remark 6 / Theorem 5(ii)) of arXiv:2607.27082
statement: "For β=1/r, the preceding theorem identifies the exact asymptotic of n·ℙ(D^→≥n), but the two firework comparisons yield only sufficient criteria. The survival and extinction constants differ by a factor of four." The survival criterion requires liminf_{n→∞} ℓ(n^r) > 1/(𝔼[η_0]κ) while the extinction criterion requires limsup_{n→∞} ℓ(n^r) < 1/(4𝔼[η_0]κ); the authors state "the full phase diagram on the critical line is not determined by the present argument."
context: On the sharp off-critical threshold β_c=1/r (survival for β<1/r, extinction a.s. for β>1/r) is established, but the behavior exactly at the critical line β=1/r is left with a factor-of-four gap between the authors' sufficient conditions for survival and extinction.
result_status: reduced, with the answer identified and one earlier claim retracted. The factor four is an artefact of the comparisons: one factor of two from using D* on both sides instead of D-> and D<-, one from the constant 1/2 in the two-sided criterion. The firework growth chain is asymptotically multiplicative with E[log U] = psi(c)+gamma, so the critical constant of the one-sided process is 1 (classical; here with an explicit drift and the subcritical exponent 1-c as the Cramer root of Gamma(k+c)Gamma(1-k)/Gamma(c)=1). For the TWO-SIDED process the criterion is max(c_R,c_L) > 1, not c_R+c_L > 2 as the first version of the memo proposed from a first-moment count of closed intervals: survival under max > 1 is a coupling (delete one side's reaches and the other side is exactly a one-sided firework), and (c_R,c_L)=(1.5,0.4) has sum 1.9 yet survives in simulation to size 1e9. Extinction under max < 1 is supported but open; the natural decoupling argument is FALSE, because a site at one end whose reach crosses the whole interval revives the other end at an order-one rate per excursion, which is also why the symmetric two-sided decay exponent is (1-c)^2 rather than 1-c (measured to within two per cent for 0.5<=c<=0.8, N up to 1e12). The critical line is then decided by E[eta]kappa lim l(n^r) against 1, and the frog-model threshold is unaffected since both sides carry the same constant.

It was refuted by an asymmetric simulation and then by a coupling that needs no numerics. Scripts h0024_fast.py, h0024_exp.py, h0024_thresh.py; the 1e15 and 1e18 columns of the threshold run are a sampler-ceiling artefact and were not used.

source_title: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs (D. Aldous and J. Fill, unfinished monograph, 1994-2002/2014)
title: An exact characterization of the relaxation time as an infimum over flows
statement: "Does there exist a characterization of the relaxation time as exactly an inf over flows?" The source notes that Chapter 4 gives an inequality bounding the relaxation time above by an inf over flows, "but it would be more elegant to derive such inequalities from some exact characterization".
context: Found by sweeping the source for every numbered open problem and comparing with what the ledgers carry. Thirteen labels were in no row: 2.34, 3.44, 4.38, 4.49, 6.13, 6.35, 7.26, 7.30, 7.31, 8.23, 14.12, 14.29, 14.31.
result_status: ANSWERED NO, for any characterization of the shape Chapter 4's bounds have. A congestion or resistance functional minimised over families of flows subject to LINEAR constraints is a linear program; a finite LP with rational data attains its optimum at a basic feasible solution, which solves a square subsystem of the constraints, so the value lies in the field generated by the data and is RATIONAL when the transition probabilities are. But tau_2 need not be: for the simple random walk on the path with SIX vertices every transition probability is 1/2 or 1 and tau_2 = 1/(1-lambda_2) = 3 + sqrt(5) = 5.2360679..., with lambda_2 = (1+sqrt5)/4 = cos(pi/5), which is the known path spectrum cos(pi k/(n-1)), so the value is confirmed against a closed form and not only symbolically. Also P5: tau_2 = 2 + sqrt(2); C5: tau_2 = 1 + sqrt(5)/5. The flow quantity of Open Problem 4.49 behaves as the argument requires: inf psi = 5 exactly on P6 and 15/4 on P5, both rational. Where tau_2 is rational (3/4 for K4, 3/2 for Petersen) it is because the eigenvalue happens to be. THE OBJECTION AND WHY IT FAILS: an infimum over flows need not be linear - Chapter 4's other flow bound is an ENERGY, a convex quadratic program. But the minimum-energy flow is the effective resistance, whose optimality conditions are a rational linear system, so it is rational too. Both flow functionals the chapter uses miss 3 + sqrt(5). WHAT IS NOT RULED OUT: a genuinely nonlinear flow functional. And the companion note to I0026 gives a characterization of exactly the right shape in a different currency: 2 tau_2 is the maximum of sum_{a,b} pi_a pi_b d(a,b) subject to sum_e pi_i p_ij d(e) = 1 over the cone of NEGATIVE-TYPE d - the same objective and the same normalisation as the dual of inf psi, over squared Euclidean distances instead of metrics. That cone is not polyhedral, which is where the irrationality lives.
verification: Author-checked only, no independent read. The proposition is elementary. The witness was computed symbolically with rational arithmetic from the transition matrix's characteristic polynomial, and lambda_2 was then confirmed against the closed-form path spectrum cos(pi k/(n-1)) - two independent routes to 3 + sqrt(5). The flow values come from the same exact linear program used for I0026, written twice and controlled against an independently written dual. The scope restriction to linear (and convex quadratic) programs is stated in the memo; a nonlinear flow characterization is not excluded, and a negative literature search is a claim about the search.

source_title: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs (D. Aldous and J. Fill, unfinished monograph, 1994-2002/2014)
title: A simple proof, and a diameter version, of an eigentime inequality
statement: "(i) Is there a simple proof of (4.49) in general? (ii) Does (4.49) hold with the diameter Delta in place of log n?"
context: Found by sweeping the source for every numbered open problem and comparing with what the ledgers carry. Thirteen labels were in no row: 2.34, 3.44, 4.38, 4.49, 6.13, 6.35, 7.26, 7.30, 7.31, 8.23, 14.12, 14.29, 14.31.
result_status: PARTIAL ANSWER TO BOTH HALVES. The key is that inf_f psi(f) is the minimum congestion of a multicommodity flow with demand pi_a pi_b and capacity c_e = pi_i p_ij, so LP duality gives inf psi = max over metrics d on V with sum_e c_e d(e) = 1 of sum_{a,b} pi_a pi_b d(a,b), and the optimal d is the shortest-path metric of its own edge values. Write B(G) = max_A 2 pi(A)pi(A^c)/Q(A,A^c) for the best CUT metric and gap(G) = inf psi / B(G) >= 1 for the flow-cut gap. Then: (1) tau_2 >= 1 for every connected non-complete graph (test function pi_v 1_u - pi_u 1_v on a non-adjacent pair makes the Dirichlet form vanish), and tau_2 = (n-1)/n < 1 for K_n, so the complete graphs are exactly the graphs of relaxation time below one and exactly the graphs of diameter one; (2) B(G) <= 2 tau_2 by the Poincare inequality with 1_A/pi(A) - 1_A^c/pi(A^c); (3) hence R = inf psi/(tau_2 Delta) <= 2 gap(G)/Delta(G), so PART (ii) HOLDS WITH CONSTANT 2 FOR ANY GRAPH WHOSE FLOW-CUT GAP IS AT MOST ITS DIAMETER, and a counterexample must be a graph whose flow-cut gap exceeds its diameter; (4) PART (i) follows at once: Leighton-Rao in the product-demand form of Linial, London and Rabinovich bounds gap by O(log n), and (2) is elementary, so inf psi = O(log n) tau_2 - a short modern proof of Sinclair's inequality in which the log n is exactly the l_1 distortion of the optimal dual metric; (5) if the uniform metric is optimal then R < 2 STRICTLY for every non-complete graph, since R = 2 dbar/(tau_2 Delta) <= 2 dbar/Delta < 2 as dbar < Delta; (6) if every BLOCK of G is outerplanar or is K4 - equivalently G has no K_{2,3} minor - then every shortest-path metric on G lies in the cut cone, so inf psi = B(G) <= 2 tau_2 with no diameter factor at all. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 after a source check: the first draft said K4-minor-free, which is WRONG. Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, Combinatorica 24 (2004), Proposition 3.1: the graphs on which every supported metric embeds isometrically in l_1 are exactly the K_{2,3}-minor-free ones (blocks outerplanar or K4), the outerplanar half from Okamura and Seymour, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 31 (1981) 75-81; series-parallel graphs only have BOUNDED distortion (their Theorem 5.11 gives 16), not distortion 1. The correction cuts both ways and is worth more than the original claim: K_{2,3} is itself series-parallel and has inf psi = 13/6 = 2.1667, B = 35/18 = 1.9444, 2 tau_2 = 2, so INF PSI <= 2 TAU_2 IS FALSE on a five-vertex series-parallel graph and the diameter factor in 4.49(ii) is doing real work. Same on K_{2,4} (gap 1.125), K_{2,5} (gap 1.162), theta(3,3,3) (gap 1.107); outerplanar graphs, K4 and eight random series-parallel graphs all return inf psi = B(G) exactly, and theta(2,2,3) does too although it has a K_{2,3} minor, which the theorem does not explain. COMPUTATION: the primal was written densely and sparsely (agree to zero relative error on 9 graphs) and the dual written separately in the pair variables with triangle inequalities (agrees with the primal to 2e-15 on 13 graphs). Over all 992 connected graphs on 4-7 vertices the optimal dual is a single cut metric in 887 cases, the uniform metric in 40, neither in 85; max gap there 1.219; max R = 2 attained only by complete graphs, largest non-complete R = 1.2083. Steepest-ascent search over edge toggles at n = 8,9,10 finds local optima near R = 1 away from the complete graph. The polarity graphs of PG(2,q) (diameter 2, lambda_2 = sqrt(q)/(q+1) exactly, mean distance -> 2) climb toward the bound from below: R = 0.849, 0.921, 1.106, 1.225 at q = 2,3,5,7 and at least 1.372 at q = 11, with R -> 2 like 2 - 2 q^{-1/2}; their flow-cut gap at q = 7 is 1.0024. Largest inf psi/tau_2 seen anywhere is 2.6 (K_{5,5}); largest gap anywhere 1.30 (K_{5,5}). Vertex-transitivity does NOT imply the uniform metric is optimal: C_12(1,2,3) has inf psi 3 against 2 dbar 8/3, and the pentagonal prism 3.6 against 3.4 (in both the cut metric is optimal instead). NOT PROVED: gap(G) <= Delta(G) in general; the worst known flow-cut gaps are bounded-degree expanders, where gap and diameter are both Theta(log n), so the conjecture is tight there up to constants and cannot be proved by any argument that discards the diameter. ADDED the same day: (7) 2 tau_2 IS THE SAME MAXIMISATION as the dual of inf psi, restricted to SQUARED differences. Writing the variance and the Dirichlet form out, 2 tau_2 = max_f [sum_{a,b} pi_a pi_b (f_a-f_b)^2] / [sum_e c_e (f_i-f_j)^2] - the same objective and the same normalisation as Proposition 1, over d(a,b) = (f_a-f_b)^2. Cut metrics are f = 1_A, so B(G) <= 2 tau_2 is a one-liner. But a squared difference is NOT a metric, so 2 tau_2 is not a feasible value of the metric program and the two are INCOMPARABLE: K_{2,3} (2.0 vs 2.1667), K_{4,4} (2.0 vs 2.5) and Paley 13 (2.5547 vs 2.7692) have 2 tau_2 BELOW inf psi, while C6 (4.0 vs 3.0), P6 (10.47 vs 5.0), the star S6 (2.0 vs 1.8), the barbell K4-K4 (17.64 vs 13.0), the lollipop K5+2 (7.02 vs 5.25) and two K4 glued at a vertex (6.0 vs 3.75) have it ABOVE; K5, Petersen and the cube are equal. THE FRAME THIS GIVES: B(G) is a sparsest-cut quantity, inf psi is its METRIC (LP) relaxation, 2 tau_2 is its SPECTRAL relaxation, and Sinclair's inequality says the two relaxations agree within O(log n) - the log n being the Leighton-Rao loss on the metric side and Cheeger's squaring the loss on the spectral side. Open Problem 4.49(ii) asks whether the diameter can replace that logarithm. The identity was verified by a generalised eigenvalue problem on the two quadratic forms, a different code path from the transition-matrix eigenvalues, agreeing to 2e-15 over twelve graphs. AUDIT 2026-09-14: every number printed in the memo was transcribed into a script (af449_audit.py) and recomputed from the graph. 107 of 107 agree, plus a negative control. THREE errors were caught and fixed before the memo shipped, none of them arithmetic. (a) The K4-minor hypothesis in Proposition 7, wrong, caught by a source check. (b) The claim lambda_2 = sqrt(q)/(q+1) 'exactly' for the polarity graphs: exact to machine precision for q = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, but OFF BY 7.9 PER CENT at q = 2, the Fano plane's seven-vertex graph, which is now stated as the exception and is the audit's negative control. (c) A quoted ratio of 2.82 for Paley 17's inf psi/tau_2, which conflated inf psi (2.8235) with the ratio (2.272); the largest ratio computed exactly is 2.6 at K_{5,5}, the atlas maximum is 2.417, and the polarity graph at q = 11 gives at least 2.743 with its program too large to finish. A FOURTH failure was procedural: one earlier text replacement silently did not match, because the search string passed through a shell heredoc that collapsed doubled backslashes and turned a LaTeX macro into a control byte, so the stale text survived unnoticed until the audit. Every later edit was made from a script file with an assertion before the write.
verification: Author-checked only, no independent read. Propositions 1-6 are elementary and written out in the memo. Proposition 7's citation was checked against the primary source on 2026-09-14 and the first draft's hypothesis was WRONG (K4-minor-free instead of K_{2,3}-minor-free); the corrected form is quoted from Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, Combinatorica 24 (2004), Proposition 3.1, and the counterexample K_{2,3} to the over-general form was then computed directly. The numerics are exact linear programs, controlled two ways (dense vs sparse primal, and primal vs an independently written dual).

source_title: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs (D. Aldous and J. Fill, unfinished monograph, 1994-2002/2014)
title: Linear Kemeny constant for distance-regular graphs
statement: "Prove that, over distance-regular graphs excluding the n-cycles, tau_0 = O(n). Of course this would imply tau* = O(n) and EC = O(n log n)." The source notes Biggs found the value 195/101 for max_{i,j} E_i T_j/(n-1) on the cubic graph with 102 vertices and outlined an argument that this may be the maximum over known distance-regular graphs, and asks in the same place whether tau_2 = O(log n) in that setting.
context: Found by sweeping the source for every numbered open problem and comparing with what the ledgers carry. Thirteen labels were in no row: 2.34, 3.44, 4.38, 4.49, 6.13, 6.35, 7.26, 7.30, 7.31, 8.23, 14.12, 14.29, 14.31.
result_status: REDUCED to an identity in the intersection array, with Biggs's value confirmed and shown to be maximal over all cubic distance-regular graphs; the conjecture itself is NOT proved. In a distance-regular graph the distance to a fixed target is a birth-and-death chain on {0..d} with down-rate c_i/k, up-rate b_i/k and stationary measure k_i/n, so tau_0 = E_d T_0 = k * sum_{i=1..d} (k_i+...+k_d)/(k_i c_i), an identity in the intersection array alone. Two consequences: the i=1 term is exactly k(n-1)/(k c_1) = n-1, so EVERY distance-regular graph has tau_0 >= n-1 with equality only for the complete graph, and the conjecture is that the remaining terms add a bounded multiple; and the excluded cycles fail precisely because k_i c_i = k for every i, making all d ~ n/2 terms of order n and tau_0 = n^2/4. COMPUTED: over the thirteen cubic distance-regular graphs (a complete classification) the maximum of tau_0/(n-1) is 195/101 at the Biggs-Smith graph, exactly the value Aldous and Fill attribute to Biggs, so that part of his outlined claim is settled - it is the maximum over all cubic distance-regular graphs, not just the ones he checked. Every classical infinite family tends to tau_0/n -> 1: Hamming H(16,2) 1.080, H(16,4) 1.023, Johnson J(50,25) 1.002, Odd graph O_15 1.078. A search over FEASIBLE intersection arrays (basic monotonicity and integrality plus the standard test that the eigenvalue multiplicities be positive integers), valency 3 to 6 and diameter to 12, finds nothing above the Biggs-Smith value; the cubic maximum over feasible arrays is again 1.9118 = tau_0/n at diameter 7, which is Biggs-Smith and is the unique feasible cubic array of that diameter. FURTHER REDUCTION, same day: putting u_i = k/(k_i c_i) and T_i = k_i+...+k_d gives tau_0/n = sum_i u_i (T_i/n), and since k_{i+1}c_{i+1} = k_i b_i the u_i satisfy u_1 = 1 and u_{i+1} = u_i (c_i/b_i), so u_i = prod_{j<i} (c_j/b_j) with no k_i in it. Hence tau_0/n = sum_i (T_i/n) prod_{j<i}(c_j/b_j) <= sum_i prod_{j<i}(c_j/b_j), and a SUFFICIENT condition for the conjecture is the purely arithmetical statement that sum_{i<=d} prod_{j<i}(c_j/b_j) is bounded over distance-regular graphs other than the cycles. Measured: that sum is between 1 and 3.5 over the thirteen cubic graphs (2.25 at Biggs-Smith, 3.5 at the dodecahedron), falls to 1 on the Hamming and Johnson families, and is exactly 2d for the n-cycle, where every ratio c_j/b_j is 1/1. A ratio is at most 1/2 unless b_j = c_j = 1, so the question is how long a run of b_j = c_j = 1 a distance-regular graph of valency at least three can have.
verification: Author checked against a computation sharing none of the same machinery: the hitting-time linear system solved for every target on the actual graph, for Petersen, Q_3, Q_4, the dodecahedron, Heawood, Pappus, Desargues, K_{3,3}, K_{5,5}, K_7, C_12 and the icosahedron - all twelve agree exactly with the identity. TWO BUGS CAUGHT BY CONTROLS, both of which a weaker check would have missed: (1) the first version used head sums k_0+...+k_{i-1} instead of tail sums and still reproduced n^2/4 on the cycle exactly, because a cycle's k_i are symmetric and cannot distinguish the two; the complete graph, where it returned 1 instead of n-1 = 3, exposed it. (2) the multiplicity test used u_i^2/k_i instead of k_i u_i^2 and rejected all thirteen cubic distance-regular graphs, which is what that control existed to catch. A third slip, an enumeration that let the valency fall below k and so admitted cycles as the extremes, was caught by requiring the enumeration to contain Biggs-Smith. Scripts drg_hitting.py, drg_check.py, drg_families.py, drg_feasible.py. Memo: Probability_I0031_distance_regular_hitting_times_2026-09-14.md The product expansion was checked against the closed form on all thirteen cubic graphs and agrees exactly on every one; an indexing slip in the recursion (using b_0 where the ratio needs b_i) was caught by that same check, which disagreed on twelve of the thirteen before the fix. Script drg_products.py.

title: Let Hk be the 2k ×2k Hadamard matrix obtained by the Sylvester construction (see above)
statement: Conjecture 13. Let Hk be the 2k ×2k Hadamard matrix obtained by the Sylvester construction (see above). For odd k, we have disc(Hk) = √ 2 √ 2k. Note that this would settle Conjecture 12. Remark 6.1 (Boolean Fourier Analysis).
context: Found by sweeping every campaign source with local text for numbered problem labels and comparing with the locator numbers of the rows carried for it; this label appeared in none.
result_status: ANSWERED, and the conjecture is FALSE. Conjecture 13 asks whether disc(H_k) = sqrt(2)sqrt(2^k) for odd k, with disc(A) = min over x in {+-1}^n of the sup norm of Ax. Writing the Sylvester matrix as (-1)^{a.u} makes H_k x the Walsh-Hadamard transform of the Boolean function whose +-1 truth table is x, so disc(H_k) = min over f of max|W_f| = 2^k - 2*(max nonlinearity on k variables), which is the covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,k). The conjectured value is exactly the bent concatenation bound 2^{k-1} - 2^{(k-1)/2}, and whether that bound is optimal for odd k is a solved question: Patterson and Wiedemann (1983) beat it at k=15 with nonlinearity 16276 > 16256, giving disc(H_15) <= 216 < 256; and Kavut, Maitra and Yucel (2006) proved that functions beating it on k odd variables exist IF AND ONLY IF k > 7. So Conjecture 13 holds exactly for k in {1,3,5,7} and fails for every odd k >= 9. At k=9 the published nonlinearity-242 functions give disc(H_9) <= 28 against the conjectured 32. CONSEQUENCE for the same list: Conjecture 12 (limsup of sup_A disc(A)/sqrt(n) > 1) loses its proposed route, though the Sylvester ratio is still strictly above 1 for every odd k because no bent function exists in odd dimension; the measured ratios are 1.237 at k=9 and at most 1.193 at k=15, both below the conjectured sqrt(2).
verification: Author checked by computation, not by citation. The three published hexadecimal truth tables of 9-variable functions with nonlinearity 242 (Kavut and Yucel, IACR eprint 2007/308 / arXiv:0808.0684) were read and their Walsh spectra computed here: max|W| = 28 for all three, i.e. nonlinearity 242 > 240, so disc(H_9) <= 28 < 32. Nonlinearity is invariant under permuting input coordinates and under complementing f, so the hex reading convention cannot affect the result. disc(H_k) was also computed exhaustively over all 2^n sign vectors for k = 1,2,3,4, giving 2, 2, 4, 4, matching the conjecture where it is true and the even-k theorem. An independent heuristic search over the rotation-symmetric class on 9 variables reached max|W| = 32 and no lower, consistent with the published account that sub-32 functions are rare. Scripts verify_242.py, disc_small.py, hadamard_disc.py, hadamard_disc2.py, pw15.py. Memo: Probability_I0092_sylvester_hadamard_discrepancy_conjecture_false_2026-09-14.md
